prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: hand-painted portrait cutout for a portfolio homepage.
Input image 1 is the edit target. Preserve this man's identity, smile, glasses, beard, pose, clothing, muted teal shirt, charcoal jacket, white tote strap, and especially the light ash-blond streaks sweeping through his dark windswept hair.
Change the rendering to a more expressive, visibly painted gouache/oil-brush illustration: distinct broad directional brush marks in the face, hair and clothing; chunky overlapping pigment patches, visible bristle trails, tactile dry-brush texture and simplified shapes. Keep the likeness and highlights clear at small web sizes. The painting must have visibly authored strokes instead of a fine pencil sketch or photographic texture.
Crucial edge treatment: the bottom of the torso must dissolve into irregular downward and diagonal dry-brush strokes that taper into transparent space. Let the lower jacket, shirt and tote break up into brush marks with decreasing opacity, ending at different heights. The lowest 15–20 percent should become increasingly sparse brush strokes and then fully transparent before the bottom edge. No straight horizontal crop across the body. A natural unfinished painting edge, not a smooth rectangular gradient. Some slight dry-brush breakup at the outside sleeve edges too.
Composition: keep the vertical 4:5 canvas and waist-up pose, full hair visible, with margins all around, including enough room below for the tapered painted edge. Entire surrounding background must be genuinely transparent alpha, no paper rectangle, no scenery, no shadow, no text, no watermark. Keep warm natural skin and the current restrained colors.
